newsitem.title: USA: LaserSight says encouraged by results.
newsitem.headline: LaserSight says encouraged by results.

text.p: LaserSight Inc said it was encouraged by the results of clinical trials in France using its excimer laser for correcting near-sightedness, or myopia.
The company said 30 myopia patients were treated from September through December 1995 and have completed up to 10 months' follow-up evaluation.

Results showed that 91 percent have retained visual acuity of 20/40 or better, the requirement for driving without correction by glasses or contact lenses. "Virtually no haze or regression appeared in patients during the long-term follow-up period," the company said.
The results of the trials will be submitted for CE Mark approval for commercial marketing of LaserSight's excimer laser in Europe, the company said.
In addition, the results will also be submitted as supplemental data to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in conjunction with LaserSight's U.S. clinical trials, it said.
